required_items.text: Resident agreement: an explanation of all charges to the resident, including security deposits if applicable.
Resident agreement: a statement that all charges, fines or penalties assessed against the resident are included in the agreement.
Resident agreement: a statement that the basic rate will not change without 30 days' written notice to the resident or, if the resident cannot understand it, to the sponsor.
Resident agreement: an explanation of the facility's policy for refunding charges on absence, discharge or transfer, and its policy for refunding security deposits.

Resident agreement: an explanation of the services offered, the types of skilled nursing care the facility provides or allows, the authorized providers, and the limits on the type and duration of skilled nursing care.
Resident agreement: an explanation of the extent and types of services the facility will provide and who is responsible for payment.
Resident agreement: a statement that the facility must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond the limits identified in (E)(5).
Policy to give residents before admission: the residents' rights policy and procedures required by ORC 3721.12.
Policy to give residents before admission: the facility's smoking policy. Rule -07 cites 3701-16-13(W), but smoking appears at 3701-16-13(U) in the current rule text.

Policy to give residents before admission: policies on advance directives and DNR orders, with an explanation of the resident's rights under state law. An advance directive or DNR order cannot be required as a condition of admission.
Information to give residents before admission: the definition of skilled nursing care from rule 3701-16-01.
For residents seeking a special care unit, the facility's policy on care in that unit. It must contain the items F(5)(a) to F(5)(l) below.
Special care unit policy: a statement of mission or philosophy that reflects the needs of the special population.
Special care unit policy: admission criteria, including screening criteria if applicable.
Special care unit policy: transfer and discharge criteria and procedures.

Special care unit policy: a weekly staffing plan if applicable. It must state how the plan differs from the rest of the facility (F(5)(d)(i)) and the necessary increase in supervision for residents with cognitive impairments or serious mental illness (F(5)(d)(ii)).
Special care unit policy: a description of activities offered (frequency and type), how they meet the unit residents' needs, and how they differ from the rest of the facility if applicable.
Special care unit policy: a listing of the costs of services the facility provides to the resident.
Special care unit policy: specialized staff training and continuing education practices.
Special care unit policy: the process for assessment and provision of services, including how services change as the resident's condition changes.
Special care unit policy: if necessary, how the facility addresses residents' behavioral healthcare needs.
Special care unit policy: the physical environment and design features that support residents' functioning.
Special care unit policy: family involvement and the availability of family support programs.
Special care unit policy: any services or procedures over and above those in the rest of the facility, if applicable.
An explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate disabled or potentially disabled residents, and its policy on transferring residents to units that accommodate disabilities.
Any other facility policies that residents must follow.

If the facility has a policy of entering into risk agreements: a written explanation of the policy and of the provisions a risk agreement may contain. It must be given to each prospective resident or sponsor, with a signed acknowledgment kept on file.

A written disaster preparedness plan to be followed in an emergency or disaster. It must be readily available in the facility and also kept electronically for off-site access. It must include J(1) to J(6) below.

Disaster plan: procedures for evacuating all individuals, including (a) provisions for residents with impaired mobility and (b) provisions for transporting all residents to a predetermined appropriate facility or facilities.

Disaster plan: a plan for protecting all persons in a fire and procedures for fire control and evacuation. This includes a fire watch and prompt notice to the local fire authority and state fire marshal when fire detection, alarm or sprinkler systems are impaired or inoperable.
Disaster plan: procedures for locating missing residents, including notifying local law enforcement.
Disaster plan: procedures for residents' health and safety in severe weather such as tornadoes and floods, and designation of tornado shelter areas.
Disaster plan: procedures, as appropriate, for facilities near areas with specific disaster potential (airports, chemical plants, railroad tracks).
Disaster plan: notification of the director by email or phone when normal business services are interrupted by an emergency or disaster involving the facility.

Drills and records: required fire exit drills and disaster preparedness drills (including a tornado drill). The facility must investigate and correct problems found. It must keep a written drill record and evaluation for three years.
Post in each section or floor a wall-specific floor plan showing room use, alarm sending stations, evacuation routes and exits, fire alarms and extinguishers, and flow of resident evacuation.
Train all staff in fire control and evacuation procedures within three working days of hire. A staff member may not be alone with residents before this training.
Annual fire prevention training for regularly scheduled staff on all shifts, with records kept.
Train all residents in the proper actions to take in a fire, tornado, disaster or other emergency.

Smoking: permitted only in designated areas. Oxygen areas are smoke-free and need 'No smoking' signs. The facility must take reasonable precautions for residents who smoke, and for outdoor smoking in bad weather. This is the content behind the smoking policy in 3701-16-07(F)(2).
Report any fire, fire damage, or illness, injury or death from fire or smoke inhalation within 24 hours to the State Fire Marshal and ODH.

Written transfer agreements with other facilities that can meet the needs of residents who must be transferred because their health or safety is, or may be, adversely affected by conditions in the facility.

Incident handling: investigate and document each incident, and keep an incident log separate from the resident record. The log must be accessible to the director and show the time, place and date, a general description, and the care provided or action taken. Also make a notation in the resident's record. This rule item is a requirement that the policies must address, not a policy by itself.

Written policies and procedures to assure a safe, sanitary and comfortable environment and to control the development and transmission of infections and diseases. These sit within an infection prevention and control program that monitors compliance with them, investigates and controls infections, and trains all staff.

Infection control program: designate one or more infection prevention and control designees. Submit their name and contact information (including email) on the ODH-prescribed electronic system within 10 days of appointment. Only part of this item was visible to me, and the designee qualifications are in sub-items such as (c).
Infection control program: a tuberculosis control plan that meets the standards in rule 3701-15-03.

Infection control program: a written surveillance plan for monitoring and tracking infections using nationally recognized criteria such as McGeer, with a data collection tool and use of the surveillance data. Later sub-items of (C)(3) and any further (C) items were not seen.

Staff orientation and training within three working days of hire, applicable to the staff member's job. It must include at least: (1) the physical layout of the facility; (2) the staff member's job responsibilities; (3) the facility's policies and procedures; (4) how to secure emergency assistance; and (5) residents' rights. The staff member may not be alone with residents until this and the fire training are done.

Annual staff training, and training as needed, to implement each resident right under ORC 3721.13(A). It must explain (1) residents' rights and the staff's responsibility in implementing them, and (2) the staff's obligation to give residents with similar needs comparable service.

Training for staff who provide personal care services: first aid within 60 days of hire; personal care training or an equivalent approved program before unsupervised care; initial and annual training for special populations (cognitive impairment, serious mental illness, and others); and eight hours of continuing education annually. Therapeutic diet staff must be dietitian-trained (F).

Hiring exclusions for direct-care positions: disqualifying offenses under ORC 3721.121(C)(1), failure to complete background check forms or fingerprints, nurse aide registry findings (Ohio or another state), and professional license discipline for abuse, neglect or misappropriation.

Personnel health policies: no work during the communicable stage of a transmissible disease unless duties and precautions minimize transmission; no work while impaired by alcohol or drugs; a pre-employment health exam within 30 days before or on the first day of work.

Resident medications: for controlled substances, the facility must comply with state and federal law and have policies and procedures in place to prevent misappropriation or theft of controlled substances. The paragraph letter was not visible in the excerpt, so confirm it in the full rule.

required_items.text: Closure notice to the director must include (1) an address where the operator can be reached, (2) a plan for transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, and (3) assurances that residents go to the most integrated and appropriate setting, taking account of their needs, choice and best interests. Notice is due at least 90 days ahead where practicable, and no less than 60 days ahead.

notes: I found no single ODH policy checklist, plan of operation or policy-review form for Ohio RCFs, so the items above come from the OAC Chapter 3701-16 sections that require written policies, plans or resident-facing documents. Ohio's initial application under OAC 3701-16-03(A) asks for administrative items only: zoning, financial solvency, ownership, floor plan, certificate of occupancy, fire and heating inspection reports, and the fee. These are excluded. ODH does not appear to review a policy manual at licensure. Compliance with the policy items is evaluated during on-site surveys, which ODH says include at least one unannounced survey in each 9- to 15-month cycle. So the manual should be organised so surveyors can find each policy by rule. Matching the order of the rules is a sensible approach, but it is not an ODH requirement. Limits of this review: (1) I could not open the April 2026 Initial License Packet or the Initial Application Instructions PDFs, so check them for any additional policy items. (2) OAC 3701-16-12 and 3701-16-09 were read only through search excerpts, and the other items in those rules were not seen. (3) I did not review other 3701-16 rules or ORC 3721.12/3721.13 (residents' rights policy and procedures, which -07(F)(1) requires), or the Assisted Living Waiver provider requirements (ODA/ODM). These rules likely contain more written-policy items, such as resident assessments, activities, dietary and therapeutic diets, records, and abuse reporting. (4) Rule -07(F)(2) cites the smoking policy at 3701-16-13(W), but the current 3701-16-13 places smoking at (U). Use (U) and confirm with ODH at liccert@odh.ohio.gov or (614) 466-7713. (5) Item IDs are the rule paragraph numbers; the same letter (for example E, K or L) appears in different rules and is distinguished by the cite. (6) Item text is condensed from the rules, not verbatim.
